Compare Several Designs Against the True Doses

Source: R/oc_compare.R
oc_compare.Rd

Judge the results of several designs against the true doses of the scenarios: how often each design selects the true MTD (designs that select an MTD) or the true OBD (designs that select an OBD), how many patients it treats there, how often it selects an overdose and how many patients it treats at overdoses, how often it selects no dose, and its average sample size and duration. The result has print() and plot() methods.

Usage

oc_compare(..., truth, overdose_cutoff = NULL)

Arguments

...

Design results, named by the design, as for oc_results.

truth

The result of oc_scenarios for the same scenarios, with the same scenario names. The DLT probabilities of every scenario must agree with those stored in the results. Designs that select an OBD need scenarios with response probabilities.

overdose_cutoff

Numeric scalar or NULL. A dose whose true DLT probability is above this value is an overdose. Defaults to NULL, the tox_limit of truth.

Value

A data frame of class c("oc_compare", "data.frame") with one row per design and scenario and the columns

design, target_type, scenario

As in oc_results.

pct_correct

Percentage of trials selecting a true MTD or OBD; NA when the scenario has none.

n_pts_correct, pct_patients_correct

Average number of patients treated at the true MTDs or OBDs, and its percentage of all the patients.

pct_overdose_selected

Percentage of trials selecting an overdose.

n_pts_overdose, pct_patients_overdose

Average number of patients treated at overdoses, and its percentage of all the patients.

pct_no_selection

Percentage of trials selecting no dose.

total_n_pts

Average number of patients per trial.

duration

Average trial duration, NA for the designs without time.

with the attribute overdose_cutoff.

Details

Every quantity is computed from the per-dose averages of the results (sel_percent and n_pts_dose), so nothing is simulated again and the results need not keep the trials. A dose is an overdose when its DLT probability exceeds overdose_cutoff by more than 1e-12.

See also

oc_scenarios, oc_results, print.oc_compare, plot.oc_compare

Examples

scen <- list(
  "Scenario 1" = list(p_true = c(0.05, 0.12, 0.27, 0.35, 0.50),
                      p_resp = c(0.20, 0.35, 0.36, 0.37, 0.38)),
  "Scenario 2" = list(p_true = c(0.05, 0.12, 0.27, 0.35, 0.50),
                      p_resp = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.30, 0.60, 0.60))
)
truth <- oc_scenarios(scen, target = 0.35, target_resp = 0.25)
boin12 <- sim_boin12_multi(target = 0.35, target_resp = 0.25,
                           scenarios = scen, n_cohort = 12,
                           cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 200, seed = 1)
boin <- sim_boin_multi(target = 0.35, scenarios = scen, n_cohort = 12,
                       cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 200, seed = 1)
oc_compare(BOIN12 = boin12, BOIN = boin, truth = truth)
#> Comparison of 2 design(s) with the true doses
#> Correct: the true MTD for designs selecting an MTD, the true OBD for designs selecting an OBD
#> Overdose: true DLT probability above 0.35 
#> 
#> Scenario 1
#>              Correct (%) Pts at correct (%) Overdose sel. (%) Pts at overdose
#> BOIN12 (OBD)        49.5               35.1               1.0             2.1
#> BOIN (MTD)          39.0               25.2              13.5             3.3
#>              No selection (%) Patients
#> BOIN12 (OBD)              0.0     36.0
#> BOIN (MTD)                0.0     33.6
#> 
#> Scenario 2
#>              Correct (%) Pts at correct (%) Overdose sel. (%) Pts at overdose
#> BOIN12 (OBD)        49.5               30.2               5.0             3.0
#> BOIN (MTD)          39.0               25.2              13.5             3.3
#>              No selection (%) Patients
#> BOIN12 (OBD)              8.0     35.2
#> BOIN (MTD)                0.0     33.6
